about: The site's own wording for the panels on the reading page. claims.json holds each quotation verbatim with the first reading's notes, verified.json the second reading's verdict and corrections. This file holds only what the page says around a quotation: what it rests on (rests), the site's own figures (site) and where those figures stop (stops), plus a short role, an introduction and the strongest points and overreach for each person, reworded into the site's writing rules. 'uses' lists figures the text quotes, each checked against the published file by scripts/build_panels.py.

kinds.inference about effect on results: A reading of the effect on results
kinds.fact about process (documentary): A fact about how the revision was run

prannoy-roy.name: Prannoy Roy
prannoy-roy.role: Psephologist and journalist, a founder of NDTV, who now presents DeKoder.
prannoy-roy.intro: In a seven-minute episode on 8 October 2026 he sets the names West Bengal left off or deleted beside the swing against the TMC, and sets the women and the Muslim electors among them beside their shares of the roll.

0.rests: He does not name the data behind the two swing figures. The comparison sets the 25 seats that lost the most names against the 25 that lost the fewest, with nothing to allow for other ways those seats differ, and the episode does not define the rate it calls the deletion rate.
0.site: West Bengal's own figures show why other differences matter. Measured by the fall in the roll, the most affected districts are Kolkata North at 27.98 per 100 and Kolkata South at 24.54, and the least affected is Purbo Medinipur at 1.64. By seat the range runs from 39.74 in Chowrangee to 0.34 in Patashpur, so the seats at either end sit in different parts of the state with different histories of voting. In Bihar, the one state where the site has fitted a model of the swing, leaving out each seat's lead at the previous election turns a slope of +0.31 into -0.83.
0.stops: The site has not fitted a swing model for West Bengal. A vote count also cannot show whether the names left off or deleted moved votes from one party to another.

1.rests: The figure matches the Sabar Institute's count as BehanBox reported it, 61.8 per cent. That count takes names left off or deleted and names held for adjudication together.
1.site: The Chief Electoral Officer's own counts give smaller shares. Women were 53.5 per cent of the 58.2 lakh names left off the draft, against 49.2 per cent of the roll, and 52.6 per cent of the fall from the 2024 roll to the roll at the 2026 nominations. They were over-represented in 21 of 24 districts.
1.stops: The Chief Electoral Officer has published no split by sex of the adjudication outcomes, so the site cannot check the larger figure.

2.rests: He does not say how the religion of the electors left off or deleted was found. It can only be guessed from names, as the Sabar Institute did. His rate comparison is consistent with his own figures, 30 lakh against 19.8 lakh. The word targeted is a claim about purpose drawn from a pattern.
2.site: The site does not classify the names West Bengal left off or deleted by religion. In Bihar, where it does, the religion of those left off is guessed from names and given as a range, because some names cannot be classified. The census share falls inside that range in 18 of 38 districts and below it in 20.
2.stops: Names give only a guess at religion, and the lists record no purpose. The site makes no claim about what anyone intended.

strongest: The shares left off the draft that he gives for Delhi, Maharashtra and Karnataka, about 33, 21 and 20 per cent, are right as reported.
He asks the Commission to explain the gaps by sex and by religion, and the site lacks that data too.
further: Saying the names left off or deleted almost doubled the swing reads a cause into a raw comparison of two groups of seats.
Saying the process clearly targeted Muslim voters asserts a purpose that the figures cannot show.
He says the millions left off will now be unable to vote, which leaves out the names put back through Form 6 and appeals.

indian-express.name: The Indian Express
indian-express.role: National daily. The investigation is by Ritika Chopra, its Resident Editor in Mumbai, and the paper later released its special issue free.
indian-express.intro: On 23 September 2026 the paper reported that two Election Commissioners had objected on record to steps taken in the Commission's name. The account rests on documents the paper holds, and it keeps the failures of process apart from the election result.

0.rests: Documents the paper holds and the site has not seen. The Commission's reply spoke of written notes and differing views and did not deny that the notes exist.
0.site: The section Inside the Commission on the process page lists each dated objection with the special issue's page number, and gives the paper's count of 14 in its text.
0.stops: The site has seen only the paper's account of the notes.

1.rests: The Form 6 declaration itself can be seen on the online form, and the paper reported it on 12 July 2026. The file notes are the paper's.
1.site: The section on Form 6 on the process page sets out the declaration and the objections to it.
1.stops: No count exists of the applications the declaration held up.

2.rests: The paper does not say which count of names it used. Its figures match Newslaundry's third test, which used the names held for adjudication from the Sabar Institute's data. In the line before, the paper says there was no evidence of the revision's role in the outcome.
2.site: The Chief Electoral Officer published no count of names left off below the state, so the site measures the fall in the roll from 2024 instead. On that measure the fall exceeds the 2026 margin in 139 of 294 seats. Seats the AITC won lost 12.38 per 100 and seats the BJP won lost 9.41, and set against their own districts the gap shrinks to 0.23 against 0.03.
2.stops: A fall larger than the margin shows that it could have decided the seat. It cannot show that it did.

3.rests: The totals match the official figures as reported.
3.site: In West Bengal 60,06,675 names were held for adjudication and 27,16,393 were found not eligible. Of the appeals, 16,10,311, or 49.3 per cent, were against a name's inclusion.
3.stops: Who filed the 16 lakh appeals against inclusion is not public. The paper says the Commission did not say.

4.rests: Documents as the paper reports them.
4.site: The process page carries the Goa sequence from the special issue, marked as press. Goa left 1,00,042 names off its draft, 8.44 for every 100 electors.
4.stops: The 97 are the paper's count, and the site holds no list of them.

strongest: It rests on dated documents. It put questions to the Commission and printed the Commission's later press note in full.
It keeps the failures of process apart from the election result in so many words.
further: Very little. Its description of the disquiet as unprecedented in scale and significance is a judgement, and the paper presents it as its own.

ravish-kumar.name: Ravish Kumar
ravish-kumar.role: Journalist and broadcaster, formerly of NDTV India, who publishes daily commentary in Hindi on his own YouTube channel.
ravish-kumar.intro: His episodes of 23 September and 1 October 2026 follow the Express investigation closely. The translations from Hindi are the site's. Where he relays a party leader's figures, the panel says whose they are.

0.rests: The count of 14 matches the Express. The paper describes them as objections to decisions taken and orders issued without the two Commissioners' knowledge, which is narrower than disagreement with the Chief Election Commissioner.
0.site: The section Inside the Commission on the process page lists each dated objection with the special issue's page number, and gives the paper's count of 14 in its text.
0.stops: The site has seen only the paper's account of the notes.

1.rests: The Express reports objections about process, about access to the roll software, Form 6 and appeals. It reports no theft of votes, and on West Bengal it says there was no evidence of the revision's role in the outcome.
1.site: Nothing on the site measures purpose.
1.stops: The lists cannot show what anyone intended, and the site does not say whether anything was stolen.

2.rests: This matches the Express account of Goa.
2.site: The process page carries the Goa sequence from the special issue, marked as press. Goa left 1,00,042 names off its draft, 8.44 for every 100 electors.
2.stops: The 97 are the paper's count, and the site holds no list of them.

3.rests: He names no source in this line. The figure matches the Express, which reports more than 13 crore names left off the draft rolls.
3.site: The site's own sum across the 31 states and union territories with a draft is 13,39,03,307 names left off. In the states that published a full split by reason, about a fifth were entered as dead. In several states the final roll is larger than the draft.
3.stops: The 13 crore are names left off draft rolls before anything was put back, and they include the dead and the duplicates. The site cannot say how many of them were eligible electors.

4.rests: This matches the state totals as reported. Of the 60,06,675 names held for adjudication, 27,16,393 were found not eligible.
4.site: The West Bengal page also gives 32,68,119 found eligible and 37,05,235 appeals pending, as reported. Only 1,607 names were restored before the poll.
4.stops: These are state totals as reported. With most appeals still pending, the site cannot say how many of the 27 lakh were eligible.

6.kind: A reading of the effect on the rolls
6.rests: Form 6 is the application for new enrolment. The declaration could delay or block an application, and the Express says applicants could not submit without answering it. No source found shows it deleting names already on the roll.
6.site: The section on Form 6 on the process page sets out the declaration and the Commissioners' objections.
6.stops: No count exists of Form 6 applications refused because of the declaration.

5.rests: He gives these as the figures of Rizwan Arshad, a Karnataka minister, from the minister's letter to the Chief Electoral Officer.
5.site: The Disputes page lists the bulk Form 7 objections reported in Karnataka, each with its source. Karnataka's own pages carry the Chief Electoral Officer's district figures only.
5.stops: The Chief Electoral Officer has published no count of Form 7s by who filed them, so the 93 per cent cannot be set against an official figure.

strongest: He follows the Express documents closely, and the figures he relays from them are right as reported.
The West Bengal adjudication figure he uses, 27 lakh, is the reported official one.
He relays a Bombay High Court bench's remarks on Goa, which are about process and can be checked.
further: He moves from the paper's findings about process to vote theft, which the paper itself does not claim.
He treats the 13 crore names left off the drafts as people erased.

yogendra-yadav.name: Yogendra Yadav
yogendra-yadav.role: Psephologist and political activist. He is one of the petitioners in the Supreme Court challenge to the Bihar revision and made submissions in person. He was with Lokniti at CSDS, is the founding national president of Swaraj India, a registered party, and convenes Bharat Jodo Abhiyan.
yogendra-yadav.intro: His main method sets the roll against the projected adult population, which catches the young adults a count of names left off cannot see. The quotations are from reports of his submissions in court and of his talks.

0.rests: His oral submission in the Supreme Court, as LiveLaw reported it.
0.site: The site uses the same kind of projection. It puts Bihar's adults at about 8.30 crore on 1 March 2026, against 7.90 crore on the roll before the revision and 7.24 crore on the draft. Across 19 states the rolls held 98.3 per cent of projected adults before the revision and 84.4 per cent on the drafts.
0.stops: A projection counts residents. In a state that sends workers elsewhere it counts adults who may be registered where they came from, and the site says so beside the figure.

1.rests: His calculation as The Wire set it out. The arithmetic holds, and the ratio of electors to adults falls from 97 to 88 per cent.
1.site: The site's figures move the same way. Bihar's draft held 7,24,05,756 names after 65,59,626 were left off in the first phase.
1.stops: Part of the gap is young adults not yet enrolled and part is error in the projection, so the site does not call the whole of it disenfranchisement.

2.rests: His figures as LiveLaw reported them, with no source given. His reason, that more men migrate and die, is his own inference.
2.site: The share matches the site's count closely, though the totals differ. The first-phase lists hold 36,39,976 women and 29,19,433 men, so women are 55.5 per cent of the names against 47.9 per cent of the roll. They are over-represented in all 38 districts and in 242 of 243 seats.
2.stops: The lists do not say why. Moves on marriage account for about half a year's worth of the excess, and the district pattern runs against that explanation.

3.rests: Said in reply to a question about 2003, when he asked the Commission to produce the 2003 order, which he said was not public.
3.site: The process page sets out what the 2025 order asked of electors, from the order itself.
3.stops: The site has not compared the 2003 instructions.

4.site: The final roll did not bear the forecast out as stated. After the draft 3,66,742 more names were deleted and 21,53,343 added, and the final roll of 7,41,92,357 was 47,72,808 below the roll before the revision.
4.stops: Disenfranchisement turns on who was eligible, and the lists record only the reason an officer wrote down.

5.rests: The Wire's account of his presentation to the Court. The article does not give his adult base, and 81 lakh plus the final roll implies about 8.23 crore.
5.site: The same method on the site's projection of 8.30 crore gives about 88 lakh adults off the final roll.
5.stops: As before, the projection counts residents.

6.outlet: PTI, as carried by ETV Bharat
6.rests: A statement of purpose made at a public meeting in Kolkata, as PTI reported it.
6.site: Nothing on the site measures purpose.
6.stops: The site makes no claim about what anyone intended.

strongest: He measures the roll against the adult population, which catches young adults that a count of names left off cannot.
He pointed out early that more women than men were left off in Bihar, and the site's count of the lists bears it out in every district.
He raised problems in the final Bihar roll, entries with junk values and apparent duplicates, that can be checked against the roll.
further: Calling it the largest disenfranchisement in the history of the world, and saying it would cross 1 crore, were forecasts. Bihar's final roll fell by about 48 lakh.
He attributes a purpose to the BJP and the Commission from the choice of states alone.

debraj-ray.name: Debraj Ray
debraj-ray.role: Economist at New York University, writing as an individual in a research note on his own site.
debraj-ray.intro: His note of 10 May 2026 asks whether the names West Bengal left off or deleted could account for the BJP's majority, and shows how the answer moves with each assumption.

0.rests: An upper bound under assumptions he states. It agrees with Newslaundry's count and with The Wire's, which reached 25.
0.site: His state totals come from the same press note the site uses. They give 7,66,37,529 electors before the revision, 58,20,899 left off the draft, 60,06,675 held for adjudication and 27,16,393 found not eligible.
0.stops: The Chief Electoral Officer has published no adjudication outcomes by constituency, so the site does not compute this bound.

1.rests: His widest bound, which counts the shifted and absent as well, flips 69 seats and leaves the BJP ten short of a majority. He argues it would need about 92 per cent turnout among those left off or deleted and about 95 per cent of them voting against the BJP.
1.site: The site's Bihar estimate works the same way. In 187 of 243 seats the runner-up could not have won even with the vote of every elector left off or deleted, and the estimates have 4 to 6 seats changing hands in both directions.
1.stops: No one knows how those electors would have voted. Where the site cannot assume it, it gives the share of votes the runner-up would have needed.

2.kind: A pattern in the names left off or deleted
2.rests: His strongest evidence of a partisan pattern. He calls it a correlation and states its limit in the same passage.
2.site: The site measures the fall in the roll, a different count. Set against their own districts, seats the AITC won lost 0.23 more per 100 and seats the BJP won 0.03 more.
2.stops: The site holds no adjudication figures by seat, so it cannot test his finding directly.

strongest: He states every assumption and shows how the answer changes with it.
He separates the names deleted after adjudication, where a partisan pattern appears, from the names booth-level officers left off the draft, where none does.
further: He sets aside the 24.2 lakh entered as dead as exclusions that can be defended. In Bihar the site found deaths entered at about 3.4 years' worth, with women over-represented, so a death on the list is what the officer wrote down, and nobody checked it.

newslaundry.name: Newslaundry
newslaundry.role: Independent news site funded by its subscribers. The analysis is by Samarth Grover.
newslaundry.intro: Its piece of 7 May 2026 runs four tests of rising strictness on the names West Bengal left off or deleted and reports how the answer shrinks.

0.rests: A count of seats where the names left off or deleted exceeded the margin, which the author calls the point where the data starts to raise questions.
0.site: Measured by the fall in the roll from 2024, the site finds the fall larger than the margin in 139 of 294 seats, taking every party together.
0.stops: A count larger than the margin measures size. It cannot show an effect.

1.rests: As published. The article adds that the TMC had won all 14 in 2021.
1.site: The site has not run this test.
1.stops: The site holds no count by seat of the names held for adjudication.

3.site: The site's figures stop at the same place.
3.stops: The lists cannot tell a correct exclusion from a wrongful one, and the Commission has not published what would.

strongest: Four tests, each stated, with the answer shrinking from 82 seats to one, and an explicit refusal to claim a cause.
further: Very little. It calls the measure based on adjudication more targeted, which describes the measure and says nothing of intent.

lokniti-csds.name: Lokniti-CSDS
lokniti-csds.role: The survey programme of the Centre for the Study of Developing Societies, Delhi. The report quoted is The Wire's, by Pavan Korada.
lokniti-csds.intro: Its survey of August 2025, 3,054 interviews in five states and Delhi, asked who holds the documents the Commission's order listed.

0.rests: Survey figures as The Wire reported them.
0.site: The site has no survey of documents.
0.stops: Lacking a document did not by itself keep anyone off the roll. In the later phases most electors were matched to the 2002 to 2005 rolls and asked for no document, and Aadhaar was later accepted on the Supreme Court's orders.

1.site: The site does not measure household income. Its All India comparisons use each state's income per head.
1.stops: The site cannot say who among those left off or deleted held which document.

2.rests: A statement of risk, hedged in the report's own words.

strongest: It is the only independent survey of who holds the documents the order listed, and it hedges its own conclusion.
further: The Wire's headline, that the revision risks disenfranchising millions, is stronger than the survey's own wording.

rahul-gandhi.name: Rahul Gandhi
rahul-gandhi.role: Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha and a Congress MP, who has led his party's campaign against the revision since the Voter Adhikar Yatra in Bihar in 2025.
rahul-gandhi.intro: The quotations come from four pieces. They are a post on his WhatsApp channel in August 2025 as PTI translated it, his press briefing in Delhi on 24 September 2026, his post on X of 5 October 2026, and the joint petition of INDIA bloc leaders to the Supreme Court as The Indian Express quoted it on 13 October 2026.

0.rests: He rests the claim on six people from Bihar he met at Sasaram on 17 August 2025, who he says voted in 2024 and were missing from the draft roll. The quotation is PTI's English translation of his Hindi post, and the line about Bahujan and poor voters being punished is PTI's reported speech. The site has not checked the six cases.
0.site: Bihar's phase 1 lists left 65,59,626 names off the draft. The lists record no caste, so the site guesses it from surnames in two ways, and the two point in different directions. In the first, Scheduled Castes were 20.0 per cent of the classified names left off against 19.65 per cent in the 2023 caste survey, and General names 34.4 per cent against 10.72. In the second, Scheduled Castes were 30.0 per cent and Muslim names 29.0 per cent. One group the lists do count was over-represented. Women were 55.5 per cent of those left off against 47.9 per cent of the roll.
0.stops: Caste guessed from names is no identification, and the bounds on every group are wide. The site records nothing about income, so it cannot say whether those left off were poorer than other electors. It says nothing about what anyone intended.

1.rests: He points to his earlier presentations on Maharashtra, Mahadevapura, Aland and Haryana and to information he says came from inside the Commission. The briefing sets out no figure behind the certainty.
1.site: Bihar 2025 is the one election after a revision that the site has modelled. More names were left off the draft than the winning margin in 174 of 243 seats, and the net fall to the final roll exceeded the margin in 124. Estimating how the electors left off or deleted would have voted moves 4 to 6 seats, some each way, and the NDA keeps its majority on every estimate. A model of the swing that allows for each seat's 2020 lead gives a slope of +0.31, with a range from -0.27 to +0.89, which takes in no effect at all.
1.stops: A count of names left off or deleted above the margin shows that they were large enough to decide a seat. It cannot show that they did. The 2024 Lok Sabha election came before the revision, and the site holds no evidence on changes to the roll before it.

2.rests: He refers to the Express investigation of 23 September 2026 into the two Election Commissioners' notes. The paper reports 14 objections, about Form 6, deletions and restorations, appeals in West Bengal and access to the roll software. It does not report either Commissioner saying the vote no longer exists.
2.site: The section Inside the Commission on the process page lists each dated objection as the paper reported it. Among them are a note of 16 May 2026 that Form 6 cannot be changed without amending the 1960 Rules and a note of 13 August calling the change unauthorised and illegal.
2.stops: The site has seen only the paper's account of the notes. His sentence is his own reading of them.

3.rests: He gives his own account of the order of events and cites no document. The quotation is from the questions near the end of the briefing.
3.site: The order of 24 June 2025 directed a Special Intensive Revision in the entire country, starting with Bihar. The joint petition he later signed alleges that no recorded decision of the full Commission authorised the nationwide revision. The Commission's press note 120 of 26 September 2026 says the order had its unanimous approval.
3.stops: The site cannot say why the revision was ordered. It holds the order and the two competing accounts of how it was approved.

4.rests: His post of 5 October 2026 cites no document. It follows his post of 1 October, which cites the Commissioners' recorded objections as the Express reported them, and it came after the Supreme Court's remark of 5 October that it had not approved any modified Form 6.
4.site: The Disputes page carries each step. The Express reported the declaration on the online Form 6 on 12 July 2026, and two Commissioners objected to it in writing. On 5 October the Chief Justice said in court that any modified Form 6 had not been approved by the Court. The Commission's press note 120 says the full Commission approved the declaration and kept it for the revision, and by 30 September it had been taken off the online form in states whose final roll was out.
4.stops: No court has decided whether the change was lawful. The site cannot say who made it, and the Commission says all its decisions were unanimous. That it was done to help the BJP is his inference, and the records show nothing about purpose.

5.rests: These are the words of the joint writ petition filed on 12 October 2026 by INDIA bloc leaders, the bloc's petition, signed by him among others, as The Indian Express quotes it. The petition says reportedly, and rests on press reports of Punjab's figures.
5.site: The figure matches the site's. Punjab's roll before the revision held 2,14,61,043 names and 20,66,635 were left off, 9.63 for every 100 electors. Of those, 5,74,568 were entered as dead, 13,56,846 as shifted, absent or other and 1,19,145 as duplicates. After the draft 7,97,263 names were added and 86,038 deleted, and the final roll of 12 October 2026 holds 2,01,00,727, a net fall of 13,60,343, or 6.34 for every 100.
5.stops: Punjab's figures came through the press, given at the end of enumeration before the draft, and the published final-roll figures do not add up exactly. The rise after the draft counts new voters too, so the site does not call it names put back.

strongest: The Punjab figure in the bloc's petition matches the count the site holds.
On Form 6 his account of the record holds. Two Commissioners objected in writing, the Supreme Court said it had approved no modified form, and the declaration was later taken off the online form.
In Bihar more names were left off the draft than the winning margin in 174 of 243 seats, so exclusions large enough to decide a result were present.
further: He says it is certain that the 2024 and later elections were rigged. The site's one model of an election after a revision finds 4 to 6 seats moving, some each way, and no change of majority.
He reads the exclusions as falling on Bahujan and poor voters. The lists record neither caste nor income, and the site's two guesses at caste from names disagree.
He attributes a purpose to the Commission and to the Form 6 change, which the records cannot show.

gyanesh-kumar.name: Gyanesh Kumar, and the Election Commission of India
gyanesh-kumar.role: Chief Election Commissioner of India since February 2025. The panel also carries statements the Commission issued in its own name.
gyanesh-kumar.intro: His words come from press conferences in August and October 2025 and his National Voters' Day statement of January 2026, as The Indian Express, The Wire and PTI reported them. The Commission's statements come from its clarification of 23 September 2026 and its press note 120 of 26 September, as The Hindu and NDTV reproduced them and as the Commission published the press note.

0.rests: The Express gives his Hindi words in Roman script with its own translation. The test he sets is whether an accuser signs an affidavit within seven days. At the same conference he did not say how many electors on the draft had submitted documents or how many foreign nationals had been found.
0.site: Bihar's draft left off 65,59,626 names for four reasons as officers entered them. Officers entered 22,32,586 as dead, 26,55,900 as shifted, 9,70,081 as absent and 7,01,059 as already enrolled.
0.stops: A reason is what the officer wrote down, and nobody checked it. Whether an affidavit is filed says nothing about whether the roll is right, and the site cannot say whether any allegation about it is true.

1.rests: He spoke at a press conference in Patna on 5 October 2025, five days after Bihar's final roll. The words are The Wire's English, and the language he spoke in was not found.
1.site: None of the reasons in Bihar's published records is citizenship. The phase 1 lists give four reasons, dead, shifted, absent and already enrolled, for 65,59,626 names. After the draft the Commission's return lists 3,66,742 deleted, 62,441 as expired, 2,12,999 as shifted, 81,334 as repeated and 9,968 with no reason stated. In May 2026 the Supreme Court directed the Commission to refer any cases it had deleted as non-citizens to the authority under the Citizenship Act. Such cases may exist, and no count of them has been published.
1.stops: The site says nothing about whether any person is a citizen. A recorded reason is what an officer wrote down, and nobody checked it.

2.rests: He spoke when the Commission announced the second phase on 27 October 2025. The words are The Wire's English. He describes the procedure the order sets out.
2.site: The order of 27 October 2025 asked for no documents at enumeration and sent notices after the draft to electors who could not be linked to the last intensive revision. Across the 21 states that have published a total, 13,06,52,476 electors kept on the drafts were sent a notice, 21.1 for every 100.
2.stops: A notice records that an elector could not be linked to the old roll or that the entry showed a discrepancy. It is no finding about citizenship, and the site never treats it as one.

3.rests: PTI quotes his statement of National Voters' Day, 24 January 2026, and NDTV quotes him saying the same on 27 October 2025. The count of appeals is the Commission's own and has not been published. Amit Shah said on 29 October 2025 that three appeals had been made against the deletions. Neither count is published, and the two may count different things.
3.site: From the Commission's return, 65,59,409 names were left off Bihar's draft, 21,53,343 were added after it and 3,66,742 deleted, and the final roll of 7,41,92,357 is 47,72,808 smaller than the roll before. The Supreme Court in May 2026 opened judicial review to people it called erroneously deleted as absent, dead, shifted or duplicate. In West Bengal, where adjudication outcomes were reported, 22,21,118 appeals were filed by people excluded, as reported.
3.stops: The site has no count of appeals in Bihar, so it cannot confirm or refute zero. An appeal needs someone who knows their name was left off or deleted and is able to file one, so a lack of appeals cannot show that the exclusions and deletions were right.

4.rests: This is the Commission's clarification of 23 September 2026, as The Hindu printed it. The same day a written statement said, in The Hindu's reported speech, that differing views are a normal part of deliberation in any institution. Press note 120 of 26 September repeats that the order and the schedules had unanimous approval.
4.site: The Commission does not dispute that the notes exist. The section Inside the Commission on the process page lists them as the Express reported them. Among them are a note of 16 May 2026 that Form 6 cannot be changed without amending the Rules, a second Commissioner's agreement on 19 May, and a note of 13 August calling the change unauthorised and illegal and directing its removal. By 30 September the declaration had been taken off the online form in states whose final roll was out.
4.stops: The notes are press reports, and the site has not seen them. The site cannot say which decisions the statement of unanimity covers.

5.rests: The sentence is from the Commission's press note 120 of 26 September 2026, which the Commission repeated on X in reply to Rahul Gandhi. It refers to the Supreme Court's judgment of 27 May 2026 on the Bihar revision.
5.site: The judgment upheld the Bihar order of 24 June 2025, which asked for a declaration in Annexure D with Form 6. In the site's reading it makes no separate finding on the declaration. The declaration two Commissioners objected to in 2026 was added later to the online Form 6. On 5 October 2026 the Chief Justice said in court that any modified Form 6 had not been approved by the Court.
5.stops: It reports the hearing of 5 October as LiveLaw reported it.

strongest: His account of the second phase, matching electors to the old rolls and sending notices to those who could not be linked, describes the procedure as the order sets it out.
The reasons he gives for exclusion include the ones the records carry, death, duplicate entries and shifting.
On the internal notes the Commission did not deny that they exist, and it said differing views are part of deliberation.
further: He names non-citizens among the names left off or deleted in Bihar, which no published count shows.
He treats the absence of appeals as proof of the roll's credibility. An appeal needs a person who knows they were left off or deleted and is able to file one.

The Commission says the Supreme Court upheld the Form 6 declaration. That goes further than the judgment as the site reads it, and the Chief Justice said on 5 October that the Court had approved no modified form.

amit-shah.name: Amit Shah
amit-shah.role: Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation and a BJP leader, who spoke for the government in the Lok Sabha debate on electoral reforms on 10 December 2025.
amit-shah.intro: The quotations come from his post on X of 29 October 2025, the Press Information Bureau's English account of his Lok Sabha speech of 10 December 2025, and The Indian Express's report of a rally at Cooch Behar on 15 April 2026. The speech and the rally were in Hindi, so those quotations are English renderings by PIB and the Express.

0.rests: The post is his own, in Hindi, and the translation is the site's. He does not say where the count of three appeals comes from. The Chief Election Commissioner said no appeal was filed against the final roll, while Shah spoke of appeals against the deletions. Neither count is published, and they may count different things.
0.site: Officers entered Bihar's 65,59,626 names left off the draft under four reasons. Of these, 22,32,586 were entered as dead, 26,55,900 as shifted, 9,70,081 as absent and 7,01,059 as already enrolled. Set against death records, the dead come to about 3.4 years of adult deaths at the right ages, though 52.0 per cent of them are women against 43.4 per cent of deaths. After the draft 3,66,742 more were deleted as expired, shifted, repeated or with no reason stated.
0.stops: The site says nothing about whether anyone is a citizen. A count of appeals cannot show who was left off or deleted, and none of the reasons in Bihar's lists is citizenship. A reason is what an officer wrote down, and nobody checked it.

1.rests: This is PIB's English reported speech of his Hindi speech, and his own words were not found. PIB's summary at the top of the same release renders the last part as selectively deleting infiltrators.
1.site: Across the 31 states and union territories with a draft, 13,39,03,307 names were left off. Of these 2,79,69,558, or 20.9 per cent, were entered as dead, 9,56,35,923, or 71.5 per cent, as shifted, absent or other, and 1,01,48,459, or 7.6 per cent, as duplicates.
1.stops: Deaths and duplicates are recorded reasons in every state, as he says. No published figure counts the names left off or deleted by citizenship, and the site does not estimate one. The largest group in the records is neither dead nor duplicate.

2.rests: This is PIB's English reported speech of his Hindi speech, and his own words were not found. PIB's body calls it the government's policy and its highlight calls it the party's. It is a statement of policy and carries no count.
2.site: The Supreme Court held in May 2026 that deciding citizenship belongs to the authority under the Citizenship Act and that declining to enrol someone does not declare that person not to be a citizen. The Commission's instructions of 14 May 2026 tell registration officers to refer suspected foreign nationals to that authority.
2.stops: The site says nothing about whether anyone is a citizen, and the revision's records carry no finding on it.

3.rests: This is PIB's English reported speech of his Hindi speech. He lists intensive revisions in 1952, 1957, 1961, 1965, 1966, 1983-84, 1987-89, 1992-95 and 2002-04.
3.site: The revisions of 2002 to 2004 are the base most states are mapped to now, which agrees with his last date. Bihar and Uttar Pradesh map to 2003, and West Bengal and Kerala to 2002. By the day he spoke, a Trinamool Congress MP had petitioned the Supreme Court in July 2025, the DMK, CPI(M), Congress and Trinamool had filed pleas heard in November, the Samajwadi Party had filed one on 9 December, and the Jharkhand and Kerala Assemblies had passed resolutions against the revision.
3.stops: The site has not researched revisions before 2002 and cannot check his list. On the current revision, the record of petitions and resolutions does not bear out the statement that no party has opposed it.

4.rests: The Indian Express gives his words in English, and The Telegraph renders the same Hindi sentence differently. The Express says he was referring to over 89 lakh names, and The Telegraph to nearly 91 lakh.
4.site: West Bengal's draft left off 58,20,899 names. Officers entered 24,16,852 as dead and 1,38,328 as duplicates. The other 32,65,719 were shifted, absent or other, and the largest part of them, 19,88,076, as shifted, so death is the largest single reason. A further 60,06,675 were held for adjudication. As reported, 32,68,119 were found eligible and 27,16,393 not eligible, with no reason published, and 22,21,118 appeals were filed by people excluded.
4.stops: No published figure counts the names left off or deleted by citizenship. Being found not eligible in adjudication is no finding that a person is a foreigner, and the site says nothing about whether anyone is a citizen.

strongest: He says the revision takes the dead and those registered twice off the roll, and the records of every state carry both reasons.
His date for the last intensive revision, 2002 to 2004, agrees with the rolls most states are mapped to now.
further: He reads Bihar's few appeals as showing that infiltrators were taken off the roll. The reasons officers recorded in Bihar are death, shifting, absence and duplicate entry, and no published figure counts anyone left off or deleted as a foreigner.
He describes the names West Bengal left off or deleted as infiltrators, though the largest reason entered there is death and no reason has been published for those found not eligible.
He says no party has ever opposed the process, though parties had gone to the Supreme Court and two Assemblies had passed resolutions before he spoke.

yogi-adityanath.name: Yogi Adityanath
yogi-adityanath.role: Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh, of the BJP.
yogi-adityanath.intro: Three of the quotations are from his speech to BJP workers in Lucknow on 14 December 2025, in his own words from the video of the speech. The fourth is from his own post on X of 5 October 2026. The translations are the site's.

0.rests: His own arithmetic in the speech. He took a population of about 25 crore and a share of 64 to 65 per cent adults to reach 16 crore who should be on the roll, and set it against the 12 crore enumeration forms collected by mid-December 2025, three weeks before the draft. The 15 crore 44 lakh is the roll of January 2025.
0.site: His 15 crore 44 lakh matches the roll before the revision, 15,44,30,092. The draft of 6 January 2026 held 12,55,56,025, close to his 12 crore. The draft was 2,88,74,067 names below the old roll, which is 2.89 crore. Set against the site's projection of 16,16,85,000 people aged 18 and over on 1 March 2026, the draft was 3.61 crore short. So his four crore sets the roll against a population projection. The roll before held 95.51 electors per 100 projected adults and the draft 77.65. The final roll of 10 April 2026 held 13,39,84,792 names, 82.87 per 100 projected adults.
0.stops: The projection counts residents, and they are not all on the roll anywhere. It takes in people registered in another state and adults who never enrolled. So a shortfall against it is no count of names left off, and 16 crore is an upper bound on who could be on Uttar Pradesh's roll.

1.rests: No source is given. He says it in the video of the speech. The Hindustan Times prints the line in English as 'Eighty-five to 90 per cent of these missing voters are ours'. The Indian Express has 90 per cent, which does not match the video.
1.site: No published record says how any elector left off votes. The site can show where the exclusions fell. They were heaviest in the towns and cities, 28.12 per 100 on the urban roll against 15.25 on the rural roll, by the Chief Electoral Officer's figures as the Hindustan Times printed them. Lucknow lost the most, 30.04 per 100. When each district's rate is spread over its constituencies, seats the NDA won in 2022 lost about 19.14 per 100 and seats the SP alliance won about 17.69.
1.stops: That small difference is about places. It says nothing about the people left off, and the site cannot say whom any of them would have voted for.

2.rests: His own account, in the video of the speech, of a visit to a district he does not name. He gives no figure.
2.site: No published figure counts the names left off or deleted by citizenship. The reasons officers wrote down at the draft are death, untraceable or absent, permanently shifted, enrolled more than once and others. Of the 8,15,996 names that came off after the draft, the press reported 2,069 recorded as under age or not citizens. On the ages he describes, electors whose link to the old roll showed a mismatch were sent a logical discrepancy notice, and the press reported 2.22 crore such notices in Uttar Pradesh. The site has found no Commission document that defines the category.
2.stops: A reason is what an officer wrote down, and nobody checked it. The site says nothing about whether any person or group is a citizen, and it cannot test what he saw on his visit.

3.rests: His own post on X of 5 October 2026, in Hindi. The same post says the dead, the permanently shifted and duplicate entries must be verified according to the rules. PTI's English rendering, carried by ThePrint, leaves out its opening words to every aware voter.
3.site: The reasons officers wrote down at the draft are almost all about people who died, moved or are listed twice, and none is named as illegal entry. Of the names left off, 16.01 per cent were entered as dead, 27.54 as untraceable or absent, 44.95 as shifted, 8.82 as enrolled more than once and 2.68 as others. The one recorded reason near his word illegally, under age or not a citizen, covered 2,069 of the 8,15,996 names deleted after the draft, as reported. The largest group deleted after the draft, 3,50,026, were people sent a notice who did not answer.
3.stops: A reason is what an officer wrote down, and nobody checked it. The figures after the draft are press reports. The site says nothing about whether anyone on or off the roll is a citizen.

strongest: His figure for the roll before the revision, 15 crore 44 lakh, is right, and his 12 crore is close to the draft of 12,55,56,025.
The roll did fall well short of the adult population. The draft held 77.65 electors per 100 projected adults, against 95.51 before the revision.
His post names the dead, the shifted and duplicate entries as what must be checked, and those are the reasons officers recorded for almost every name left off.
further: His gap of four crore sets the roll against a population projection, and the projection counts residents who are not all on the roll anywhere. Against the old roll the draft was 2.89 crore smaller.
Saying 85 to 90 per cent of those missing are his party's voters goes beyond any record, since nothing published says how an elector left off or deleted votes.
Tying the exclusions to names entered illegally goes further than the officers' own records, which give under age or not a citizen as the reason for 2,069 names after the draft, as reported.

mamata-banerjee.name: Mamata Banerjee
mamata-banerjee.role: Chairperson of the All India Trinamool Congress, and Chief Minister of West Bengal when the revision began there.
mamata-banerjee.intro: The quotations come from four reports between November 2025 and September 2026. They are a Bengali report of her speech at the end of a march in Kolkata, her letter to the Chief Election Commissioner as The New Indian Express printed it, and two speeches as reported in English. The translation from Bengali is the site's.

0.rests: The Commission's order of 27 October 2025, which named twelve states and union territories for the second phase and left out Assam and the North-East. Her words are in Bengali, from News18 Bangla's report, and the translation is the site's.
0.site: The point about the process held when she said it. Assam was given a Special Revision by the Commission's order of 17 November 2025, with no enumeration forms and no link to an earlier roll, and it has never had an SIR. In that revision 10,56,291 names were flagged as dead, shifted or multiple. The North-East came later. The order of 14 May 2026 put Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Arunachal Pradesh, Sikkim and Tripura in the third phase, and Tripura's enumeration ran from 15 September to 14 October 2026, with its draft due on 21 October.
0.stops: The site's records cannot test her claims about fake votes in Assam or about who crosses into India through Tripura. Nothing the site holds counts entries by nationality, and it says nothing about whether any person or group is a citizen.

1.rests: Her letter of 20 November 2025, as The New Indian Express printed it. She posted the letter as an image, and The Telegraph's version paraphrases it.
1.site: Three months is about right for the schedule as first ordered. Enumeration in West Bengal ran from 4 November to 4 December 2025, later extended to 11 December. The draft came on 16 December, and the final roll, first due on 7 February and then on 14 February, was published on 28 February 2026. That is about four months from the first house visit to the final roll, and the 60,06,675 names put under adjudication were decided after it. The site's list of deaths reported during the revision has two items from West Bengal, both reported after this letter.
1.stops: The site holds no record of how long earlier intensive revisions took, so it does not check her three years. It does not count deaths.

2.rests: No list is given in the report, which is PTI's account of her speech at Red Road in Kolkata, carried by The Hindu. The English is the agency's, for words she may have spoken in Bengali. Her figure rose over the weeks. On 2 December 2025, announcing Rs 2 lakh for each family, she gave 39 deaths.
2.site: No official count of deaths linked to the revision has been published. The site's list of deaths reported during the revision has eight items across India. Two are about West Bengal electors called to hearings. One is a 75-year-old man who fell ill in a hearing queue in Birbhum, in a report that also mentions an elderly man who died at a hearing in Howrah. The other is an 82-year-old man in Purulia whose son filed an FIR after he died, allegedly by suicide, hours before a hearing. Each is a press report of what a family alleged.
2.stops: The site cannot say how many people died, or why, so neither 110 nor three to four a day can be checked here.

3.rests: No source is given in the report. She spoke at a rally in Serampore in Hooghly, likely in Bengali, and the English is The Indian Express's.
3.site: The 93 lakh is near the site's figures, depending on what is added. The draft left off 58,20,899 names, and 5,46,053 more came off on Form 7 after it. Of the 60,06,675 put under adjudication, 27,16,393 were found not eligible and 32,68,119 eligible, as reported. The draft, Form 7 and those found not eligible add to 90,83,345, about 91 lakh. Below the state the site has the fall in the roll, 77,58,998 from the 2024 roll to the roll the 2026 election was held on. That fall was larger than the winning margin in 139 of 294 seats, and larger than the margin at the seat's turnout in 132.
3.stops: The adjudication outcomes are state totals as reported. Below the state the site has only the fall in the roll, never the names left off. Larger than the margin means those names could have decided a seat, never that they did, and nothing in the records shows why the revision was run.

strongest: Her question about Assam rested on a real difference in process. Assam had a Special Revision with no enumeration forms, and the North-East was added to the SIR only in May 2026.
Her 93 lakh is close to the site's own sum of names left off at the draft, deleted on Form 7 and found not eligible after adjudication, 90,83,345, as reported.
Three months is about right for the enumeration, the draft and the claims as first ordered.
further: Saying the SIR was run to capture the state is a claim about purpose, and nothing in the records shows why it was run.
Her count of more than 110 deaths, and three to four a day, rests on no published list. The site's own list of reported deaths has two items from West Bengal.
Saying the BJP wins Assam on fake votes is something no record the site holds can test.

reporters-collective-up-ceo.name: The Reporters' Collective and the Chief Electoral Officer of Uttar Pradesh
reporters-collective-up-ceo.role: The Reporters' Collective is an investigative newsroom that has reported on the SIR in several states. Navdeep Rinwa is the Chief Electoral Officer of Uttar Pradesh, the official responsible for the state's electoral roll.
reporters-collective-up-ceo.intro: The Collective reported on 9 October 2026 that the Commission's software produced 85,854 objections to delete Uttar Pradesh electors with no reason given, and followed it on 14 October with the Chief Electoral Officer's answers. This panel sets the two reports beside his answers, as the Collective and IANS printed them, beside his February count, and beside the Commission's order of 9 October capping objections as the press reported it. The Chief Electoral Officer's video and his first post on X were not available to the site, so his words are given as those outlets printed them.

0.rests: The Collective's own scrape of the Form 7s shown on the Chief Electoral Officer's website. The scraped file is not published.
0.site: Uttar Pradesh's draft of 6 January 2026 left off 2,88,74,067 of the 15,44,30,092 names on the roll before it. After the draft, 8,15,996 names were deleted, as the press reported the Chief Electoral Officer's figures, and 3,50,026 of them were people who did not answer a notice. The site holds 2,68,682 Form 7s filed from 6 January to 6 March 2026.
0.stops: The site has no count of Form 7s after 6 March and none of forms filed by officers, so it cannot check the 85,854. How many of the 8,15,996 deletions went through a Form 7 has not been published.

1.rests: Interviews with four election officials whom the Collective does not name, and the pattern in its scraped forms. No document from the software is published.
1.site: Notices went to 3.26 crore of the electors on the draft, 1.04 crore with no link to the old roll and 2.22 crore for discrepancies, as the Chief Electoral Officer told The Times of India. Of those deleted after the draft, 3,50,026 had not answered their notice. The Chief Electoral Officer's office has said that notices, hearings and orders came before every deletion, and it has not denied that the software produced the forms.
1.stops: The site has no record of how ERONET works or of who signed which form.

2.rests: The same scrape, read against the end of the claims and objections period. The report does not say which date it took as the deadline, and the likeliest is 6 March 2026.
2.site: The site's count of Form 7s in Uttar Pradesh is 2,68,682, from 6 January to 6 March 2026. The final roll came on 10 April 2026 with 13,39,84,792 electors.
2.stops: The site cannot say which Form 7s were filed late or what became of them.

5.rests: His own count of names that drew more than one Form 7, with no source given. The words are from his recorded video of 9 October 2026 as the Collective quotes them, and the video was not available to the site.
5.site: His 13.39 crore is the final roll, 13,39,84,792 electors. The Collective sets his 4,700 against its finding of more than 200 attempts to delete names in bulk across the state, which were objections filed by individuals and are a separate matter from the 85,854 forms. In February he gave 4,336 deletions from objections filed by other people, which counts deletions where this counts names objected to.
5.stops: The site has no count of names that drew more than one Form 7.

6.rests: The office's account of its own procedure, with no figures. IANS reported it from Lucknow on Tuesday 13 October 2026. The Collective describes an earlier post on X, minutes after its report of 9 October, which used different words, and that post was not available to the site.
6.site: The statement answers how the forms were described and gives no count of them. After the draft, 8,15,996 names were deleted, as the press reported the office's figures. Of these, 3,50,026 did not answer a notice, 3,28,960 were entered as shifted, 79,076 as multiple entries, 55,865 as dead and 2,069 as under age or not citizens.
6.stops: The office has not published how many of those deletions went through a Form 7 and how many through a notice, so the site cannot say.

7.rests: His running count to 16 February 2026, eight weeks before the final roll, as The Times of India quotes him.
7.site: The draft held 12,55,56,025 electors. By the final roll, 8,15,996 names had been deleted after the draft, as the press reported his office's figures.
7.stops: The site has the end figure only as the press reported it, and nothing between February and April.

8.rests: PTI's account of the Commission's letter of 9 October 2026 to Chief Electoral Officers. News On AIR, Deccan Herald, Deccan Chronicle, DT Next and Outlook report the same limit. None of them prints the letter, and it was not available to the site.
8.site: Every report of the order found gives 10 objections per elector during a claims period and five a month at other times. The Collective's report of 14 October says the order allowed no more than 30 objections a month, which matches no other report and cites no document.
8.stops: The site holds no count of Form 7s per objector.

strongest: The count comes from the Chief Electoral Officer's own published forms, with a stated denominator (85,854 of 87,127) and dates, so anyone with the same pages could repeat it.
The Chief Electoral Officer's office answered how the forms were described, and no report found has it disputing the number.
further: The Collective writes that he confirmed its finding. That rests on what he did not say in the video, since it quotes no sentence in which he confirms the count.
The limit of 30 objections a month in the follow-up matches no other report of the Commission's order, all of which give 10 per elector during a claims period and five a month afterwards.
The account of how the software produced the forms rests on four officials the Collective does not name.

drop.3: It rests on religion guessed from names.

bjp.name: The Bharatiya Janata Party
bjp.role: India's governing party. Its account of the SIR figures here comes from two videos on its official YouTube channel, posted in October 2026.
bjp.intro: Only the videos' titles and descriptions were available to the site. What is said in them and shown on screen was not, so the quotations are from the descriptions, and no speaker is named in either.

0.rests: The Commission's counts of names left off the drafts, by the reason recorded beside each.
0.site: Across 31 states, 13,39,03,307 names were left off the drafts. Of these, 9,56,35,923 (71.4%) were entered as shifted, absent or other, 2,79,69,558 (20.9%) as dead and 1,01,48,459 (7.6%) as duplicates. The party's figures agree with these to the precision it gives.
0.stops: A reason is what the officer wrote down, and nobody checked it. In Bihar, set against death records, the names entered as dead come to about 3.4 years of adult deaths at the right ages, but 52.0% of them are women against 43.4% of deaths.

2.rests: The Commission's letter of 1 October 2026 to every Chief Electoral Officer.
2.site: The letter orders booth officers to compare the roll from before the revision with the current one, visit those missing from it at home and help those found eligible fill in Form 6.
2.stops: No figures from the drive have been published, and the site has none.

3.rests: The Commission's stated purpose for the revision, and Bihar's final roll.
3.site: Bihar's final roll of 30 September 2025 held 7,41,92,357 electors, which rounds to 7.42 crore. The Commission's total for June 2025 was 7,89,69,844, so the roll fell by 47,77,487 over the revision. 65,59,626 names were left off the draft and 3,66,742 deleted after it.
3.stops: The sentence gives the end figure and leaves out the fall. The site counts names on the roll and cannot say who among those left off was eligible.

strongest: Its split of the 13 crore by recorded reason is the Commission's own and agrees with the site's totals.
It is right that the 13 crore are names left off the drafts by recorded reason, and some were restored afterwards.
further: The split is offered as an answer to whether eligible electors were left off. The reasons are what officers wrote down, and the largest group, shifted, absent or other, cannot show whether those electors had moved.
The Bihar sentence gives the final roll of 7.42 crore and leaves out the fall from about 7.89 crore before the revision.

abhijeet-dipke.name: Abhijeet Dipke
abhijeet-dipke.role: Founder of the Cockroach Janta Party, which has led protests in Mumbai and Delhi since 2 October 2026 calling for the Chief Election Commissioner to resign.
abhijeet-dipke.intro: The quotations come from his press conference at the Press Club of India in New Delhi on 15 October 2026, held with AISA's Neha Bora the day before the party's march at Connaught Place, as PTI reported it, and from an earlier press conference on 24 September 2026 as Business Today reported it. The party's own recording is on YouTube. PTI's Hindi service rendered his word 'setting' as मिलीभगत (collusion), and which language he spoke in is not recorded.

0.rests: The Commission's counts of names left off the drafts, set against the national gap in vote share between the two alliances in 2024. In the same report PTI put the NDA at around 43 per cent of the 2024 vote and the INDIA bloc at around 40.6 per cent.
0.site: Across the 31 states with a draft roll, 13,39,03,307 names were left off the drafts, 14.08 per 100 of the 95,08,13,771 on the rolls before. By the reason recorded beside each, 2,79,69,558 (20.9%) were entered as dead, 1,01,48,459 (7.6%) as duplicates and 9,56,35,923 (71.5%) as shifted, absent or other. His 14 per cent is right to the precision he gives. In the 22 states whose final rolls are out, 7,77,48,303 names were left off of 65,67,36,949 (11.84 per 100), and the net rise after the draft brought back at most 14.6% of them.
0.stops: A reason is what the officer wrote down, and nobody checked it. The site holds no party vote shares, so it does not check his 2 per cent. The 2024 election was held on the rolls from before the revision, which was ordered on 24 June 2025, so the names left off had no part in the 2024 result.

1.rests: The size of the count against a national gap in vote share. He offers no other evidence of purpose.
1.site: Elections are decided seat by seat. Spread evenly over each state's Lok Sabha seats, the names left off exceed the 2024 winning margin in 373 of 516 seats in those 31 states, and 115 of the 542 contested seats were won by fewer than 50,000 votes. The even spread is an assumption, and in Tamil Nadu it gives 27 seats over the margin against 19 counted seat by seat. In Bihar the names left off came more from booths that voted NDA in 2024 (49.0% against 37.8% INDIA), and the estimate there is that 4 to 6 seats change hands, in both directions.
1.stops: The rolls record names and reasons. They cannot show why anything was done, and the site makes no claim about purpose.

2.rests: The Commission's counts of names left off the drafts, as he gave them on 24 September 2026.
2.site: Across the 31 states with a draft roll, 13,39,03,307 names were left off the drafts, 14.08 per 100 of the 95,08,13,771 on the rolls before. By the reason recorded beside each, 2,79,69,558 (20.9%) were entered as dead, 1,01,48,459 (7.6%) as duplicates and 9,56,35,923 (71.5%) as shifted, absent or other.
2.stops: These are names left off the drafts, and some came back afterwards. Most were never votes cast, since the count includes the dead and duplicate entries and the roll holds people who do not vote.

3.rests: No figures are given in the report, which adds that he provided no evidence for the claim.
3.site: Kerala's Chief Electoral Officer published no table of names left off. Measured as the fall in the roll from January 2025, the roll fell by 6,67,990 by the election (2.40 per 100), and that fall was larger than the winning margin in 38 of 140 seats, or 30 when taken at each seat's turnout. In Dharmadam, his own seat, the roll at the election was larger than in January 2025, 2,06,000 against 1,98,819, and the CPI(M) held the seat by 19,247.
3.stops: A fall larger than a margin shows that it could have decided a seat, never that it did. The site does not model how those left off would have voted in Kerala.

strongest: His count is right. 13,39,03,307 names were left off the drafts, 14.08 per 100 on the rolls before.
The names left off are large against close seat margins, which is the strongest form of his point.
further: The 2024 election came before the revision, so the names left off could not have shaped its margin. The comparison works as a warning about the next election.

The 13 crore are names left off the drafts by recorded reason, among them the dead and duplicate entries, and some came back on the final rolls. Calling them votes deleted goes further than the figures.

A national gap in vote share is a share of votes cast, and the names left off are a share of the roll. Seats are the measure that decides results, and the seat figures here show the names left off large enough to decide many seats, never that they did.
Setting is a claim about purpose, which the rolls cannot show. In Bihar, where the site has modelled the effect, it runs both ways.
The Kerala claim goes further than the fall in the roll. Dharmadam's roll grew, and the CPI(M) held the seat.

s-y-quraishi.name: S.Y. Quraishi
s-y-quraishi.role: Chief Election Commissioner of India from July 2010 to June 2012.
s-y-quraishi.intro: The quotations come from one post of his on X, of 2 October 2026, about the Commission's letter of 1 October that sends booth level officers to help people no longer on the roll apply through Form 6. Free Press Journal reported the post the same day, and Newslaundry put the point to the Commission on 5 October.

0.rests: The 2022 amendment to the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960 (S.O. 2802(E) of 17 June 2022), which titled Form 6 “Application Form for New Voters” and made rule 13(1) speak of a claim “as new elector”.
0.site: He is right that the Rules and the form are written for new electors. No document read says a person whose name was deleted or left off may not file it. Section 23(1) of the Representation of the People Act, 1950 lets any person whose name is not on the roll apply, Form 6 is the only form for that, and the Commission's Manual on Electoral Rolls of March 2023 says a person no longer on the roll has to apply again through Form 6. A Commission official told Newslaundry there is no other route. Across the 31 states with a draft roll, 13,39,03,307 names were left off the drafts, and Form 6 is the way back for all of them who were not restored by an appeal.
0.stops: The site does not count how many people filed Form 6 after the revision.

1.rests: Item (iii) of the Form 6 declaration, “I am applying for inclusion in Electoral Roll for the first time”, which the form gives no way to strike out, read with section 31 of the 1950 Act.
1.site: The form supports him on one line. A person who was on a roll before cannot truthfully say they are applying for the first time, and the Commission has published nothing on how such a person should answer it. Section 31 punishes only a statement the person knows or believes to be false, or does not believe to be true, and its penalty is up to one year in prison, a fine or both. No court ruling or prosecution for signing that line to get back on the roll has been found. On 14 October 2026 the Delhi High Court closed a petition by two electors left off Delhi's roll. It said one petitioner's fear of being accused of a false declaration if he filed Form 6 was misplaced, because the Commission's standing counsel had suggested Form 6 on the Electoral Registration Officer's instructions. The order does not mention item (iii) or section 31.
1.stops: Whether anyone committed an offence is for a court. The site can set out the text of the form and the Act and nothing further.

2.rests: The Commission's letter of 1 October 2026, which he calls a press note. It tells booth level officers to visit people who were on the roll before the revision and are not on it now, and to help them enrol through Form 6 where they are eligible.
2.site: The letter does direct officers to help people file Form 6, and the direction is older than the revision. The Commission's Manual, from instructions of 2021, already told officers that a person whose name was wrongly deleted could submit a Form 6. The Commission's letter and its officers' role are set out on the process page.
2.stops: Abetment needs an offence, and no document shows one was committed. The site makes no claim about anyone's purpose.

strongest: The form's own wording supports him. Since 2022 Form 6 is titled for new voters, and its declaration asks every applicant to say they are applying for the first time, with no way to strike the line out.
The Commission has published no guidance on how a person who was on the roll before should answer that line, while sending its officers to ask such people to fill the form.
further: Section 23(1) of the 1950 Act lets anyone not on the roll apply, and Form 6 is the only form for it, so a deleted elector is not barred from filing it.

Section 31 needs a statement the person knows or believes to be false. Saying all who filled the form committed an offence goes further than the Act, and no court has ruled on item (iii). The Delhi High Court has called one elector's fear of a false-declaration charge misplaced where the Commission's counsel had suggested he file Form 6.
Calling officials abettors needs an offence to abet, which no document shows.

p-chidambaram.name: P. Chidambaram
p-chidambaram.role: Member of the Rajya Sabha for the Congress and a former Union Minister of Finance and of Home Affairs.
p-chidambaram.intro: The quotations come from one post of his on X, of 16 October 2026. He wrote it the morning after the Commission was reported to have ordered a special summary revision of the rolls in 17 states and union territories, and the Supreme Court issued notice on the INDIA bloc leaders' petition against the Commission. The News Mill carried the whole post the same day, with inputs from ANI.

0.rests: The order for a special summary revision, as ANI and PTI reported it on 15 October 2026, and the Supreme Court's notice of the same day on the INDIA bloc leaders' petition.
0.site: Both events are real and fell on the same day. None of the reports of the order (ANI, PTI as carried by Siasat, and The News Mill) gives a reason tied to the protests or the notice. As reported, the order covers the 17 states and union territories where the revision is over, with Assam, which had a Special Revision, so it stops nothing that was running. The Commission had already said on 26 September 2026, before both notices, that the revision was complete in 20 states and union territories, and it ordered a drive to enrol people left out.
0.stops: The rolls and the order as reported give no reason for its timing, and the site makes no claim about why the Commission acted.

1.rests: The Commission's letter of 15 October 2026 ordering a special summary revision with 1 January 2027 as the qualifying date, as ANI and PTI (through Siasat) reported it.
1.site: The number 17 is the order's. As reported, the 17 are the states and union territories where the revision is over, with Assam, which had a Special Revision instead. All 16 others have a final roll, the latest Punjab's of 12 October 2026. PTI's copy says that in these 17 states the special intensive revision is over and calls the summary revision annual. For the states still in the revision, ANI reports that the schedule will be announced separately, and no report or document found says the revision has stopped anywhere. Ten states and union territories are still in it, nine awaiting a final roll and Tripura with no draft yet. Six that have finished, Odisha, Arunachal Pradesh, Sikkim, Mizoram, Chandigarh, and Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu, are outside the 17, and the reports do not say why.
1.stops: The site holds no copy of the order and no schedule for a summary revision in the states still in the revision.

2.rests: His reading of the change to a summary revision. He names no document, and no report of the order mentions documents of citizenship.
2.site: The documents point the same way for new applicants. In the revision a declaration went with every Form 6, first the Bihar declaration of 24 June 2025 with its documents by year of birth, then the declaration of 27 October 2025, which asks for an entry in the roll of the state's last intensive revision. The Commission said on 26 September 2026 that outside the revision the forms of the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960 apply. PTI reports there will be no house-to-house visits in the summary revision. The revision did not ask every elector for documents either. From its second phase none were collected with the enumeration form, and notices went to those who could not be linked to the old roll.
2.stops: The site has not seen the order of 15 October 2026 or any instruction on what a Form 6 applicant must file in the summary revision, and the order may say more than the reports carry.

4.rests: A count of the names left off the draft rolls in the revision. He gives no source.
4.site: Across the 31 states with a draft roll, 13,39,03,307 names were left off the drafts, 14.08 per 100 of the 95,08,13,771 on the rolls before. His 13.30 crore is about 9 lakh below that. Of those names, 2,79,69,558, about one in five, were entered as dead, as he says. The 20 states finished by 26 September 2026 account for 7,48,54,691, and the other 5.9 crore are in 11 states that had not finished by then, nine of which still await a final roll. A name left off the draft has not been deleted. The Supreme Court held for Bihar that leaving a name off the draft “is not tantamount to a final deletion, but is only a provisional step”. Deletion is an order of the registration officer under section 22 of the 1950 Act, after a reasonable opportunity of being heard, with an appeal under section 24. After the draft, 33,65,116 names were deleted in the 20 states that published those figures. On Bihar the Court held that the deletions were not contrary to the procedure of Rule 21A and that the safeguards of notice and hearing were preserved in substance.
4.stops: The site counts names. It cannot say whether a hearing was given in any case, or how many of those left off were entitled to stay. The Court's judgment is on Bihar, and the later phases are before it in petitions now pending.

5.rests: The drive for electors left out, announced on 26 September 2026 and set out in the Commission's letter of 1 October, and the summary revision ordered on 15 October as reported.
5.site: The drive exists. On 26 September the Commission said anyone whose name had been left out during the revision or after may apply, and told its officers to launch a special drive to enrol them. The letter of 1 October tells booth officers to compare the roll from before the revision with the current one, visit those missing and help those found eligible fill in Form 6. In the 22 states with a final roll, the roll rose by 1,13,76,238 on net between draft and final. That is at most 14.6% of the names left off there, and the rise counts new voters too.
5.stops: The site holds no count of Form 6 applications from the drive. The word illegally is his. The one judgment so far, on Bihar, held the deletions there within the procedure of the Rules, and the later phases have not been ruled on.

strongest: His 20 is the Commission's own count of states and union territories where the revision was complete on 26 September 2026, and the site's records give the same 20 on that date.
His 13.30 crore is within one per cent of the 13,39,03,307 names left off the drafts in 31 states, and about one in five of them were entered as dead, as he says.
The Commission did order a drive to bring back people left out, on 26 September and 1 October 2026, and has now ordered a summary revision with the same aim.
Outside the revision the Commission said the forms of the Rules apply, so the declaration the revision attached to Form 6 should not go with one in the summary revision.
further: The 17 states in the order are where the revision is over. The reports say the schedule for the states still in it will be announced separately, and nothing found says it has been abandoned anywhere.
The order as reported gives no reason, and the drive for people left out was ordered on 26 September, before both notices. Why the Commission acted is his reading.
He sets 13.30 crore against 20 states. Those 20 account for 7.49 crore, and the rest are in 11 states that had not finished by 26 September, nine of which still await a final roll.

Names left off the draft have not been deleted, and the Supreme Court held Bihar's deletions consistent with the procedure of the Rules. “Without Due Process” and “illegally” are his charges, and no court has ruled on them for the later phases.
No report of the order says documents of citizenship need not be produced. That is his inference, though the Commission's note of 26 September points the same way for new applicants.
